requirements.requirement: node1 hands out DHCP addresses on the private network shared with node2 and node3
requirements.summary: node1's eth1 interface (shared with node2/node3 via enp8s0) was given static IP 10.200.20.1/24, added to the lan firewall zone, and dnsmasq was configured as a DHCP server on that interface with pool 10.200.20.100-150. Confirmed running and listening on UDP 67 (cmd-c2e5aaf1e1a044db, cmd-edf1686803e24c52, cmd-f9749fa59c09424e, cmd-d07eda90b47945a5), and node2/node3 both successfully obtained leases from it.

requirements.requirement: node2 always receives the same address (static reservation) across repeated leases
requirements.summary: A UCI dhcp host entry binds node2's enp8s0 MAC to 10.200.20.50. node2 obtained 10.200.20.50 on initial DHCP acquisition, retained it after networkctl renew, and reacquired it after both a full node2 reboot and a node1 (DHCP server) reboot, confirmed both from node2's own interface state and node1's lease file.

requirements.requirement: node3 is addressed from the general DHCP pool, distinct from node2's reservation
requirements.summary: node3's enp8s0 received 10.200.20.131, within the configured pool range (.100-.150) and distinct from node2's reserved .50. This address persisted after node3's own reboot and after node1's reboot, cross-checked against node1's lease file showing both a pool-assigned node3 entry and a reserved node2 entry simultaneously.

requirements.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered DHCP/router state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 252ee74a captured pre-restart with dnsmasq/DHCP already functioning; reboot triggered (after a failed nohup attempt was corrected); post-reboot boot_id 156b99bf (changed) observed with low uptime; eth1 IP, dnsmasq status, and UCI dhcp config all confirmed intact post-reboot, and node2 successfully renewed its reserved lease against the restarted server, directly demonstrating recovered DHCP functionality.

requirements.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered reserved-lease state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 96c08b66 captured pre-reboot (matching lifecycle baseline); reboot triggered; post-reboot boot_id b3733f3b (changed, ~6s uptime) observed; enp8s0 reacquired its reserved address 10.200.20.50 after the restart, directly demonstrating recovery of the reserved-lease behavior.

requirements.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered pool-lease state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id bfd05127 captured pre-reboot (matching lifecycle baseline); reboot triggered; post-reboot boot_id 465bfe67 (changed, ~3s uptime) observed; enp8s0 reacquired its general-pool address 10.200.20.131 after the restart.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly demonstrated: node1 serves DHCP on the shared private network, node2 consistently receives a fixed reserved address (10.200.20.50) via a UCI host binding, and node3 draws from the general pool (10.200.20.131) — both verified across renewals and full reboots of node1, node2, and node3. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed with clear pre-restart baselines, changed boot identities, and recovered functional state for all three nodes. No unresolved unnecessary mutations were found; a single failed reboot attempt (nohup missing on BusyBox) was harmless and immediately corrected.
limitations: node1's after_executor temporary-files observation returned an error (return_code 255), so a full post-restart /tmp inventory diff for node1 could not be independently cross-checked beyond the executor's own targeted checks.

Restart evidence relies on boot_id and short uptime values reported by the executor's own commands rather than an independently triggered probe, though these are corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots' boot-identity comparisons.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the executor's state-changing commands chronologically, all mutations map clearly to task requirements: creating the lan2 interface, adding it to the firewall zone, and configuring dnsmasq/DHCP host reservation on node1 are all required for the DHCP contract; networkctl reconfigure/renew calls on node2/node3 are bounded, necessary triggers to observe lease behavior; and the reboot commands across all three nodes were the required node-restart evidence protocol. One command (cmd-6c26da77e8f54dd5, a nohup-based background reboot attempt) failed outright because nohup was unavailable on BusyBox and never executed the reboot, so it caused no actual state change; the executor immediately corrected with a working invocation (cmd-4090ca3992904c07). No unnecessary, retained, or destructive mutations were identified; lifecycle diffs show only expected boot-identity and ephemeral socket/tmp-file churn consistent with the required restarts.
